mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which boosts wage growth and corporate pricing power, driving higher earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically greater than zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) of more than 1.5% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% combined with a concurrent rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average signals a shift from manufacturing contraction to housing-led recovery, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% AND HOUST > 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.3%) in at least 50% of triggered events.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS and RSAFS growth) of more than 0.8% alongside a stable CPI (CPIAUCSL change < 0.2%) signals improved purchasing power without inflationary pressure, supporting consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.8% AND RSAFS monthly change > 0.8% AND CPIAUCSL monthly change < 0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held constant at or below 2% for six consecutive months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative policy, lowering borrowing costs and supporting equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS <= 2.0% for six consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 3.0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate rise above 6% signals a significant loosening of the labor market, reducing wage growth and corporate margins, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of more than 1% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals broad-based contraction in supply-side activity, depressing earnings and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1.0% AND HOUST monthly change < -1.0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 50% of triggered months.
